summary: On 14 December 2020 an automated quota system cut the quota of Google's User ID Service to zero because an old system reported its usage as zero. Authentication failed for almost every Google service for about 50 minutes.

overview.background: Google's User ID Service stores account identifiers and credentials used for OAuth tokens and cookies. It was being moved to a new quota management system.
systems: User ID Service and its account database
Google Cloud Console, BigQuery, Cloud Storage
GKE, networking control plane, Cloud Monitoring
overview.impact: From 03:46 to 04:33 PST credential issuance and account lookups failed for all Google user accounts, and nearly all authenticated traffic returned 5xx errors. BigQuery streaming saw about 75 percent errors and Cloud Storage about 15 percent of authenticated requests failed.
overview.severity: A global authentication outage of about 47 to 50 minutes. Google does not give a formal severity.
overview.gaps: The page's own times differ slightly (header 04:07 to 06:23, summary 47 minutes, preliminary 50 minutes).

diagrams.title: A quota of zero blocks the account database
diagrams.caption: The User ID Service was registered with a new quota system, but an old system kept reporting its usage as zero. When the grace period ended, the automated system cut its quota.

diagrams.caption: Google planned to review quota automation to stop fast global changes and to improve resilience of the account database writes. This picture shows the idea.

timeline.e: The User ID Service is registered with the new quota system. Parts of the old system keep reporting usage as 0.
The root cause and a potential fix are identified.
Quota enforcement is disabled in one datacenter.
The same mitigation is applied to all datacenters.
Most Google Workspace services are fully recovered.
The networking control plane is fully recovered.

rootCause.trigger: The grace period on quota enforcement ended and the automated system reduced the User ID Service's quota.
rootCause.underlying: The old system still reported that service's usage as 0, and the quota for the account database fell so the Paxos leader could not write. Reads became outdated and the service rejects requests with outdated data.
contributing: Safety checks did not cover zero load reported for a single service
The quota change applied globally and quickly
Internal support tooling was also affected, delaying updates

evidence.label: The security design
evidence.body: For security reasons, this service will reject requests when it detects outdated data.

evidence.label: What kept working
evidence.body: Cloud Service accounts used by GCP workloads were not impacted and continued to function.

evidence.label: A simulated safety check
evidence.body:
if reported_usage == 0 and historical_usage > 0:
    raise NeedsHumanReview('zero usage on a service with traffic')
evidence.note: A teaching example of the missing check. Not Google code.

diagnose.step: Compare reported usage against real traffic for critical services.
diagnose.why: A zero against real traffic is the clue.

diagnose.step: Look at quota changes and grace periods.
diagnose.why: A grace period expiry matched the start time.

correct.step: Disable quota enforcement for the affected service.
correct.why: Google disabled enforcement at 04:22 in one datacenter, then everywhere.

correct.step: Use an alternative channel for updates.

verify.step: Watch error rates return to normal.

verify.why: Workspace, networking and Calendar recovered later.

prevent.step: Review quota automation to prevent fast global changes.

fix.safety: Disabling quota enforcement removes a protection. Use a time limit and a plan to turn it back on.

troubleshoot.scenario: Every login on your platform fails at 03:46. The identity database cannot write and the quota for it was cut an hour ago.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do first and what permanent fix would you propose?
troubleshoot.answer: Disable quota enforcement for the identity service, confirm writes and reads recover, then add checks for zero reported usage and staged quota changes.

options: A grace period ended while the old system reported usage as zero
rootcause.why: Google explains the migration between quota systems.

remediation.answer: Block automated quota cuts if reported usage is zero but traffic was above zero in the last day.
Apply quota changes to one location first and bake before the rest.
Keep a status channel independent of the affected identity system.

design.prompt: Design quota changes that cannot take down a core dependency.
design.answer: Dual-read usage and compare, alert on mismatch, stage changes, keep floors for critical services and test the cutover.

checks.q: How long did the main issue last?
Why did the database reject requests?
options: It detects outdated data and rejects requests for security
Cloud service accounts used by GCP workloads
checks.why: Google says those continued to function.

preventive: Resilient writes in the identity database
practices: Do not let a single dependency block everything
